title: Ethereum FOMO grows as Bitcoin, XRP sentiment weakens – Why it matters
summary: Does bearish sentiment dominates Bitcoin, Ethereum and XRP as prolonged declines weigh on investor confidence?
content: Ethereum is experiencing growing FOMO among investors while sentiment surrounding Bitcoin and XRP weakens. Observers are closely watching how these shifting market moods might impact future price trends and trading activity for these major cryptocurrencies.

title: Interledger Foundation Takes Its First Steps to Bring Instant Payments to Community Lenders
summary:
The Interledger Foundation (ILF) is working with five community development financial institutions (CDFIs) and fintech organizations to lay the groundwork for instant payments adoption across community lending, where most institutions still run on rails that take days to settle. Large financial institutions have leveraged instant payments for years, accessing and deploying funds faster. Community-based lenders, though, have lagged, held back by technical, regulatory and resource barriers. Through five projects, Interledger Foundation is mapping those barriers to develop a roadmap that gives CDFIs and the borrowers they serve access to the same infrastructure.
FedNow, the Federal Reserve's instant payment rail, lets financial institutions send and receive funds in seconds around the clock. While large banks have adopted it steadily, CDFIs, which have deployed $272 billion in cumulative financing to underserved communities, have been far slower to connect, with most still relying on infrastructure that settles in days rather than seconds. That gap means borrowers face loan disbursements that don't arrive when they need cash most and payment friction that pushes small businesses toward less favorable options. The regulatory environment is also shifting with the Federal Reserve's proposed skinny master account, a limited-access account that would include direct FedNow and Fedwire connectivity. If that eligibility broadens, it would give those institutions a direct route onto instant payment rails.
Against this backdrop, ILF is coordinating an initiative across five community-based financial institutions to map what blocks the sector from reaching instant payment infrastructure and what becomes possible when those blocks are removed. The five organizations include:
Village Micro Fund — Connecting cooperative finance to modern payment rails. Village Micro Fund is examining whether cooperative finance models, including investment clubs and community savings pools, can be connected to modern payment rails without requiring participants to interact with cryptocurrency. The organization is researching how its platform, EnDAO, which allows community groups to pool and manage money with shared governance, can integrate with ACH, wire transfers and FedNow.
Kiva — Understanding whether frictionless payments would serve the community. Kiva is examining whether frictionless payments would change outcomes for Native entrepreneurs and Tribal communities, rather than assuming they would. Working with Native entrepreneurs, Tribal partners and Native-serving organizations, Kiva is conducting listening sessions to understand the barriers to affordable capital those communities face before making any technology decisions.
Access to Capital for Entrepreneurs (ACE) — Examining the link between payment infrastructure and credit qualification. ACE is exploring how open payments infrastructure can feed real-time cash flow data into its borrower portal in Georgia, building more secure, bank-connected payment functionality into its loan approval and repayment experience. The longer-term goal is underwriting approaches built on borrowers' real-time cash flow rather than historical averages, shifting criteria and making capital more accessible to borrowers historically marginalized by financial institutions.
Washington Area Community Investment Fund (WACIF) — Mapping the repayment friction that instant payments could solve. WACIF is researching how entrepreneurs whose cash flow doesn't follow predictable monthly patterns experience the current loan repayment system, identifying where more flexible, real-time payment options could reduce the friction that pushes otherwise viable businesses toward default.
AltCap — Building a modernization roadmap for post-closing payments. AltCap is building a modernization roadmap for post-closing payments for underserved small business owners in the Kansas City region, combining direct borrower feedback with an assessment of real-time payment options to produce a concrete plan for infrastructure improvement.
These projects are the first domestic application of the work Interledger Foundation has done since focusing internationally for years. Interledger Foundation's work centers on building the connections that allow payment systems to talk to each other, regardless of bank or network. Historically, it has applied that expertise to community-based financial institutions in Uganda, rural community banks in Mexico and payment ecosystems across Africa. This initiative extends that work to domestic community lending, where the same principles that have connected institutions abroad can address the payments infrastructure gap that has kept CDFIs and their borrowers off the same rails that large financial institutions have used for years.
"Community-based lenders have long operated on payment infrastructure that was never designed with them in mind," said Chris Lawrence, Chief Program Officer at Interledger Foundation. "This initiative gives us the opportunity to understand precisely where those barriers are and ensure CDFIs are positioned to use the same instant payment rails that larger institutions have accessed for years, so the borrowers they serve can more seamlessly access financial services."
The findings from these five projects will feed directly into Interledger Foundation’s roadmap for community lender adoption of instant payment infrastructure, shaped by the borrowers and communities it is designed to serve. This cohort of organizations is only the first step in the organization's ongoing initiative to work with community-based financial institutions.

title: Chargebacks911 Taps Kount Founding CEO Brad Wiskirchen to Accelerate M&A and Global Expansion
summary:
Chargebacks911, the global leader in chargeback processing and dispute management technology, today announced the appointment of Brad Wiskirchen, Founding CEO of Kount, as Chief Commercial Officer (CCO) of Chargebacks911 and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of its financial institution-focused sister brand, Fi911.
The high-profile appointment signals an ambitious new chapter for Chargebacks911.  Wiskirchen will spearhead strategic M&A initiatives, pursue high-value partnerships and expand relationships with financial institutions, payment processors and payment orchestration providers worldwide.
His appointment builds on Chargebacks911’s established global infrastructure, extensive industry connectivity and expanding portfolio of AI-native technologies, creating new opportunities to accelerate scale, diversify capabilities and unlock growth across the payments ecosystem.
“Brad’s appointment is about more than expanding our leadership team.  It’s about accelerating what’s next,” said Monica Eaton, founder and CEO of Chargebacks911. “We’ve spent years building the technology, infrastructure and industry relationships that have positioned Chargebacks911 at the center of an increasingly important part of the payments ecosystem. The opportunities ahead extend well beyond traditional dispute management, and we're bringing together the talent, capabilities and strategic relationships to pursue them at scale.”
Wiskirchen brings more than two decades of experience building, scaling and commercializing financial technology businesses. As Founding CEO of Kount, he helped transform the company from a true startup into a globally recognized fraud prevention technology provider, culminating in its acquisition by Equifax and Wiskirchen’s appointment to General Manager of Equifax Digital Solutions. 
Wiskirchen also served as an industrial partner at CVC Capital Partners, a global private equity and investment firm, where he led the fintech investment efforts in North America.  Additionally, Wiskirchen was named Chairman of the Salt Lake City Branch of the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, as well as a member of the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) Interdepartmental Working Group on Finance and Technology, High-Level Advisory Group. 
Wiskirchen has also served on numerous for-profit and non-profit boards in the payments, fraud, identity and compliance spaces, and he has co-founded and invested in many other businesses in those spaces.
"Brad has unmatched entrepreneurial acumen, understands the investment landscape and brings the commercial instincts and relationships to help us capitalize on opportunities that can meaningfully expand our reach,” said Benjamin Bridwell, President of Chargebacks911. “We're not simply looking to grow our existing business. We're looking to reshape what's possible across the payments ecosystem."
A key component of Wiskirchen’s mandate will be expanding the company’s presence across the financial institution sector as CEO of Fi911, Chargeback911’s dedicated sister brand serving issuing banks, acquiring banks and other financial services providers. Fi911 extends Chargebacks911’s core dispute management competencies into the financial institution market, providing tools for dispute processing, workflow automation, compliance monitoring, reconciliation and operational intelligence.
“What Monica and the team have built is remarkable, and I see enormous potential in what comes next. I haven’t seen a more impressive foundation of technology, industry connectivity and market reach,” said Wiskirchen. “I've spent my career building and scaling technology companies, and it's rare to find a business with this combination of proprietary technology, established market reach and opportunity for expansion. Chargebacks911 has already built the foundation. Now we have an opportunity to dramatically accelerate its scale through strategic acquisitions, new partnerships and expansion into adjacent markets. The convergence of AI, payments intelligence and financial services is creating extraordinary opportunities, and I believe Chargebacks911 is uniquely positioned to capitalize on them. I'm excited to work alongside Monica and the leadership team to help build the next chapter of this company's success.”
Wiskirchen’s contributions to technology and entrepreneurship have earned numerous accolades, including recognition as an Idaho Business Review ICON and an induction into Idaho’s Technology Hall of Fame in 2023.
“Brad brings the rare combination of entrepreneurial experience, investment perspective and deep industry relationships,” Eaton added, "We share a belief in challenging conventional thinking and building businesses that make a lasting impact. I couldn't be more excited about what we'll accomplish together - and it's an added bonus to welcome another fellow Idahoan to the team.”
The next generation of payments technology won't be defined by isolated solutions. It will be built by connecting intelligence, infrastructure and capabilities across the entire transaction lifecycle.

title: Continent 8 and FuturePath AI Launch Future8 Accountable AI for Regulated Industries
summary:
Continent 8 Technologies and FuturePath AI today launched Future8, an AI-native operating company built for regulated operators, formed as a joint venture between the two companies. 
Announced at SBC Summit Lisbon, Future8 combines FuturePath’s enterprise AI applications platform with Continent 8’s licensed global operating footprint, enabling the iGaming industry to deploy auditable AI without compromising compliance, data sovereignty and operational control. 
Built for highly regulated environments, Future8 enables operators to move from AI experimentation to production deployment by embedding governance, approvals and auditability into every workflow from day one. 
Continent 8 brings licensed data centers and a private global network spanning more than 100 locations, built over 28 years serving the biggest iGaming and online brands, along with AI-enabled Global Capability Centers in India, the Philippines and Bulgaria. The company also contributes operational expertise, jurisdictional knowledge and intelligence derived from one of the industry’s largest collections of regulated infrastructure and operational data, helping Future8 tailor AI solutions to the operational realities of the iGaming sector. 
FuturePath brings a production enterprise AI applications platform, with pre-built AI applications powered by coordinated agents, already running enterprise operations for Fortune 500 companies across multiple industries. Together, the companies are adapting proven enterprise AI to the workflows, controls and operating realities unique to iGaming. Unlike generic agent frameworks or toolkits, FuturePath delivers regulator-ready AI applications designed to solve real business challenges for licensed operators. 
Accountability First, Infrastructure Flexible 
Until now, the iGaming sector has faced a difficult dilemma: how to deploy AI at scale while maintaining the strict, policy-aware explainability that licensing bodies demand across every jurisdiction they operate in. Regulators have moved past asking only where data sits. They now ask how a decision was made, a question AI raises and infrastructure alone never did. 
Future8 is built to make that evidence automatic. Because its advantage is regulatory standing rather than physical location, it holds whether a workload runs in a Continent 8 facility, in a public cloud region, or in the operator’s own account. 
This allows organizations to standardize AI governance across jurisdictions while retaining flexibility in where and how workloads are deployed. 
“Everyone has AI. Almost nobody can run it in a regulated market,” said Mike Small, CEO of Continent 8 Technologies. “Future8 lets operators optimize their business and achieve efficiencies with AI that regulators can actually audit, in every jurisdiction they hold a license.” 
“Our AI applications – coordinated agents executing real business work – already run real operations inside Fortune 500 enterprises, with every action governed and auditable,” said Saurabh Bhatia, CEO of FuturePath AI. “Continent 8 brings 28 years of regulatory standing that no AI company can replicate. Together, we are building the AI application and accountability layer licensed industries will need to run AI in production.” 
Flexible Delivery, Any Stage of AI Maturity 

No two iGaming operators run the same way, which is why Future8 is built to deliver outcomes rather than tools alone. 
Future8 is designed to meet organizations wherever they are in their AI journey. They can engage through advisory services, managed AI-operated services or direct platform deployment, allowing them to adopt AI at a pace that matches their operational and regulatory requirements. 
Its services are organized into three offerings that meet operators at any stage of AI maturity, from first assessment to full deployment: 
AI Readiness Assessment for Regulated Industries. A structured evaluation of the operator’s estate, its automation opportunities, and the license conditions that govern them, concluding with a joint executive readout that maps where AI can be deployed and how it will be evidenced. 
Managed AI-Operated Services. Future8 assumes the operational workload through a global delivery network, staffed onshore, nearshore, or offshore according to what each jurisdiction requires, so coverage follows the license. The operator pays for outcomes, and the work automates down over time. As automation increases, operators benefit from improved efficiency and faster execution while maintaining the governance and controls regulators require. 
Platform Subscription. For organizations that prefer to run AI in their own environment, Future8 licenses the AI applications directly, layered with the jurisdictional policy, control, and evidence artifacts that make them acceptable to a regulator. 
The platform can be deployed within Continent 8 infrastructure, public cloud environments or customer-owned environments while maintaining consistent governance controls. 
Future8 builds on FuturePath’s field-tested enterprise AI, already proven in Fortune 500 environments, where AI applications, powered by autonomous agents, handle tens of thousands of complex workflows monthly and reduce resolution times by up to 40%. Forward Deployed Engineers work alongside operators to adapt and deploy it to their specific workflows, systems, and regulatory requirements. 
Across the iGaming industry’s business, Future8 spans IT and technical operations, cloud migration, finance and procurement, and player-facing operations, with every workflow governed, auditable, and evidenced to the regulator. 
Whether deployed as software, consumed as a managed service, or delivered through a hybrid model, Future8 combines AI technology, operational expertise and regulatory oversight into a single offering. 
Future8 launches with an initial focus on regulated iGaming, with a longer-term vision to support additional licensed industries where governance, auditability and compliance are essential to AI adoption.

title: TransUnion and Bankrate Expand Partnership to Power More Personalized Credit Offers for Millions of Consumers
summary:
TransUnion announced today that it is making it easier for millions of Americans to find personalized credit offers that meet their needs. The company's new innovation delivers smarter matching by combining Bankrate's lender marketplace with TransUnion's credit data and Monevo offers technology.
Building on more than a decade of collaboration with Bankrate, the capability gives consumers a more personalized experience and helps lenders and publishers reach consumers with more relevant offers. Consumers can access the offering today in TransUnion Credit Essentials, a free credit app and web experience that helps consumers take control of their financial health.
"Consumers have many credit choices and not enough clarity," said Steve Chaouki, President, U.S. Markets, TransUnion. "By combining TransUnion's data with our Monevo offers platform and Bankrate's lender partnerships, we've built a capability that makes offers more precise. Credit Essentials is our first proof point, and we'll bring this to many more experiences where consumers and lenders meet."
Bankrate's broad network of lender relationships and its marketplace and auction technology put lenders in real-time competition for consumers, so matches cover more products, more providers and more competitive offers. Monevo draws on multiple sources, including credit data, alternative data and consumer intent signals. Its decisioning engine then matches each consumer with highly personalized credit offers from a broad panel of lenders. Consumers see offers that can fit their needs, so they can choose with clarity and confidence.
Because partners can embed the capability through a seamless, low-lift technical integration, consumers can access personalized offers wherever they make financial decisions. It’s available today in Credit Essentials and can extend to publisher and affiliate sites, co-branded experiences for financial institutions and brands and AI assistants, where more consumers now start their search for credit.
TransUnion Credit Essentials Gaining Momentum
Millions of consumers have registered for Credit Essentials since its May 2025 launch, with membership growing approximately 50% in the last year alone. TransUnion's Q3 2026 Consumer Pulse study shows that more than half of Americans (53%) check their credit report at least monthly, and nearly all (93%) believe monitoring their credit report is important. Among consumers who check their credit report, one in 10 do so to learn which credit offers they may qualify to receive.
Credit Essentials gives consumers free daily access to their TransUnion credit report and score, real-time alerts about critical changes, credit education and personalized credit offers across credit cards, personal loans, mortgages, home equity, auto refinance, insurance and savings accounts, all in one place.
"Bankrate and TransUnion have helped consumers make smarter financial decisions for years," said Matt Fellowes, CEO, Bankrate. "TransUnion's data and identity insights, combined with Bankrate's lender relationships, auctions and marketplace, help consumers find the right products with confidence."
Credit Essentials is the first of many experiences the combined capability will power. TransUnion and Bankrate are exploring more product types to extend the offers to publishers, partners, lender platforms and AI-driven channels.
